title: fix(chat): restore first turns in a new session store
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the first message to a cold configured session store failing before any provider request. This also breaks the parent turn in the heartbeat store-lifecycle product test before it can spawn a child.

## User Impact

The first turn can create its configured store and continue with the request's original authorization. Source replacement, credential revocation, and membership changes retain their existing refusal behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regression from #169622 (`cbc53ac75eca`): native reply admission followed its own first-store registration, but the Gateway request's separate retained sharing witness did not. The witness invalidated itself on that registration.

Forward the existing committed registration callback through reply admission to that witness, after updating the admission selector and before public observers run. Keep asynchronous preparation and the reduced database work; add no SQL, retries, fallback reads, or new lifetime owner. Group the existing session-initialization callbacks in their small owner module while preserving their dispatch-time read. Schema, stored data, and update behavior stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current-main baseline and the same run under four CPU workers: 0/2 original product cases pass; the parent makes zero provider requests.
- Extended existing cold-admission regression fails before the production fix and passes after it, while retaining the no-main-thread-SQL and cleanup assertions.
- First repaired focused run: 46/46 tests pass across the original product file, sharing preparation, and admission/retention controls.
- Final version under the same CPU pressure: 2/2 original product cases pass, including child execution and notification ownership across both store transitions. `pnpm test src/gateway/server.heartbeat-store-lifecycle.product-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 179.73s Vitest, 194.65s wrapper including worker preparation; timing is not a performance comparison.
- Final binding/dispatch lifecycle run: 95/95 pass (304.50s wrapper), including credential and membership revocation.
- Final core types, targeted Gateway/infrastructure test types, lint, boundary lint, formatting, line caps, import-cycle checks, and independent P2 review pass.
- Full architecture and source-contract commands pass. All three deadcode export scans pass with zero entries. Broad affected-suite and complete check-changed proof belong to PR CI under the current local-proof policy. No remote lease was used.

The first PR CI run caught a type-only import cycle in the callback extraction. The follow-up removes the recorder import while preserving the exact six-field initialization type. Corrected Madge, core types, lint, and P2 review pass; runtime behavior is unchanged, so the completed behavior tests are reused. Corrected-head CI [38330353532](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38330353532) passes all 76 jobs at `b024cd13b300`.
